title: Priority Tenant Slicing and Burst Credit Economics
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines the Priority Tenant Slicing (PTS) model and the associated Burst Credit Economics used by Redwood's platform to allocate shared inference capacity across tenants. It covers the architecture, configuration parameters, SLO mappings, dashboards and alerts, operational runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings from the 2025 pilot, and a short roadmap for 2026 improvements.

Goals

- Provide predictable latency and throughput guarantees for paying tenants while maximizing GPU utilization for bursty workloads.
- Make trade-offs explicit: how credits, queues, and eviction policies translate to tenant experience and cost.
- Provide observability and automated remediation to keep SLO exposure below 2% of request traffic.

Scope

In-scope:
- Serving clusters in Dedicated and Hosted modes where multiple tenants share GPU pools.
- Queueing, token-based burst credits, and priority slice assignment logic implemented in the traffic router service (traffic-router).
- Billing signals and export to cost engine for invoicing and optimization suggestions.

Out-of-scope:
- Private on-prem deployments where tenant isolation policies are controlled by customers.
- Long-running batch jobs (handled by batch-runner).

Key Concepts

- Slice: A logical fraction of a GPU pool assigned to a tenant class (gold/silver/bronze/ephemeral). A slice is defined by concurrency, token/sec budget and preemption cost.
- Burst Credit: Token-like currency that allows a tenant to exceed its steady-state slice allocation for short periods. Credits recharge over time.
- Fair Window: Time window over which we measure token consumption to enforce fairness and compute credit drains.
- Preemption Penalty: Cost applied (in credits and in logging/alerting) when a tenant's in-flight requests are preempted to satisfy higher priority work.

Architecture Overview

The PTS system spans three services: traffic-router, slice-manager, and credit-orchestrator.

- traffic-router: Maintains per-tenant queues, enforces concurrency and token budgets at request admission. Tagged requests include slice-id and credit-check headers.
- slice-manager: Responsible for creating and reconciling slice assignments based on capacity signals from gpu-pool-manager and policies stored in config-service.
- credit-orchestrator: Tracks account-level credits, recharge schedules, and interacts with billing to consume or refund credits post-request (e.g., user-initiated cost shield).

Runtime flow (text diagram):

1) Ingress -> traffic-router checks slice assignment.
2) traffic-router evaluates steady-state budget and burst-credits for tenant.
3) If allowed, request proceeds to model-proxy -> serving-runtime. Otherwise, request is queued or rejected.
4) Preemption events trigger credit-orchestrator adjustments and alerts.

Configuration Reference (table represented as CSV for concise embedding)

slice_tier,concurrency_limit,tokens_per_minute,credit_recharge_rate,preemption_penalty
GOLD,200,120000,60/min,50
SILVER,80,48000,30/min,30
BRONZE,20,12000,10/min,10
EPHEMERAL,5,3000,5/min,5

Sample policy YAML (used by config-service):

policy_name: default-2026
slices:
  - name: GOLD
    concurrency: 200
    rpm: 120000
    recharge_rate: 60/min
    preemption_penalty: 50
  - name: SILVER
    concurrency: 80
    rpm: 48000
    recharge_rate: 30/min
    preemption_penalty: 30

SLOs and Mapping

- GOLD: 99th percentile < 60ms tail added latency (router+serving-runtime) under 90% steady-state load. Error budget: 0.5% monthly.
- SILVER: 95th percentile < 150ms under 80% steady-state load. Error budget: 1% monthly.
- BRONZE: 95th percentile < 300ms under 60% load. Error budget: 2% monthly.

Operational Dashboards and Alerts

Dashboards to create in Grafana (panel groups):
- Slice Health Overview: per-slice QPS, avg queue depth, token consumption rate, current credits.
- Preemption & Throttling: preemptions/min, throttled_reqs/min, top 10 tenants by preemptions.
- Cost-distribution: per-tenant token consumption, estimated GPU-seconds attributed, credit balance heatmap.
- Serving Impact: 99p latency for GOLD vs cluster baseline, CPU/GPU utilization.

Critical alerts (PagerDuty)
- ALERT A1: slice-gold-credit-depleted -> triggers when GOLD slices across any gpu-pool have <5% aggregate credits and throttling > 2% of requests for 5m. Severity: P1. Playbook: emergency scale or temporary promote credits (see runbook).
- ALERT A2: preemption-spike -> preemptions increase >x5 baseline in 2m window. Severity: P2. Playbook: investigate upstream noisy tenant and rollback recent config changes.
- ALERT A3: router-queue-growth -> avg queue depth > 2000 requests for >10m. Severity: P1. Playbook: traffic reroute to warm pools or enable burst limits.

Runbooks

Runbook: GOLD credit depletion (P1)
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty.
2) Check Grafana slice health and credit-orchestrator dashboard.
3) Run: curl -s "https://internal-api/slice-manager/v1/pools?pool=live" | jq '.pools[] | select(.slice=="GOLD")' to identify affected pools.
4) If overall utilization < 80%: execute temporary-credit-topup job: POST /credit-orchestrator/v1/topup {"slice":"GOLD","amount":100000} (requires ops-admin).
5) If utilization > 90%: follow emergency-scale playbook: expand pool (terraform apply -var 'pool_size=+2') and promote warm standby nodes. Notify finance for temporary cost exception.
6) Communicate to customers via status page and update internal incident tracker with action and ETA.

Runbook: Router queue runaway (P1)
1) Identify offending tenant(s): query traffic-router metrics: top_queue_tenants over last 10m.
2) If ephemeral tenant consuming >50% of queued requests, set ephemeral tenant slice to EPHEMERAL-throttle via config-service.
3) If multiple tenants: enable circuit-breaker at ingress to shed non-paying traffic.
4) Reconcile: set slice-manager to rebalance slices and monitor for 15m.

How-to: Tune recharge rates for bursty workloads

1) Collect 7-day histogram of token consumption per tenant and median inter-arrival.
2) Compute target recharge_rate = peak_burst_tokens / desired_recovery_window_minutes.
3) Simulate via staging traffic-router with new policy YAML and run load test using loadgen and 'replay-bursts' scenario.
4) Iterate until tail latency meets SLO and credit depletion events are under threshold.

Billing and Cost Signals

- Credits consumed are asynchronously exported to the cost engine as events (credit-consumed). Each event includes tenant_id, slice_id, tokens_consumed, gpu_seconds_estimate, and charge_code.
- For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, credits act as surge billing and are reconciled monthly. For hosted customers, credit policies are tied to plan and metered at per-token price.

Retrospective (2025 pilot)

What went well:
- Pilot reduced cold-start throttling by 18% by using warm standby pools and short burst credits.
- Dashboards gave early warning signals; we caught a noisy-tenant pattern before SLA violations.

What we learned:
- Initial recharge rates were too aggressive for LLM workloads with long decoding tails; we needed to tie recharge to sequence-length-weighted tokens.
- Preemption logging lacked request-level correlation ids; we instrumented traffic-router to add trace_id and request_seq to preemption events.

Actions taken:
- Adjusted credit accounting to weight tokens by decoded sequence length.
- Added structured preemption events to eventstream and wired to Sentry and tracing.

Roadmap (Q1–Q4 2026)

- Q1: Automated adaptive recharge: credit-orchestrator uses ML-derived recharge schedules per tenant class.
- Q2: Per-model quantization-aware slice: allow slices to declare quantization profiles to better estimate GPU-seconds per token.
- Q3: Cross-region credit migration: allow credits to float between regions for multi-region tenants.
- Q4: Tenant-facing credit insights in Console; self-serve top-ups and forecasted spend alerts.

Notes and Open Questions

- Q: Should preemption_penalty be billable to tenants who cause preemptions? Recommendation: during pilot keep penalty as visibility-only. Consider billing changes after 6 months of monitoring.
- Q: How should sequence-length weighting interact with caching (prefix cache)? We propose cached tokens count as 0.2x for recharge calculations; measurement required.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets

- List pools by slice: 
  curl -sS https://internal-api/slice-manager/v1/pools | jq '.pools[] | {pool, slice, utilization}'

- Replay burst test (local):
  go run ./tools/loadgen --scenario replay-bursts --tenant $TENANT --duration 10m --qps 500
